utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the witness make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Andolina. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Excellencies. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Dr. Andolina. Did you give a statement to my Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D05009 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Andolina, do you see on the screen in front of you your statement?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And have you read the statement and did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page so that Dr. Andolina could identify his signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I identify my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And since that time, since the 18th of August, 2009, has anything changed in your professional life?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes. From -- since one year I retired. So I am a retired old physician.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this statement faithfully reflect what you told the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Andolina, if I were to put the same questions to you today in this courtroom that were put to you when you were giving the statement, would your answers in essence be the same?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I would like to tender this bundle pursuant to 92 bis [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objections, Ms. Iodice?

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's recorded on the transcript "92 bis." I assume Mr. Karadzic said "92 ter."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Andolina. Yes. We'll admit the Rule 92 ter statement as well as the associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The statement 65 ter number 1D5009 will be Exhibit D3005, and 1D5010 will be Exhibit D3006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like to read the summary of Dr. Andolina's statement in English. [In English] Dr. Marino Andolina is a doctor from Trieste, Italy, specialising in bone marrow treatment for children. In 1993, Dr. Andolina began travelling to the former Yugoslavia to provide medical assistance to children in need of bone marrow treatment. During one trip, he travelled to the Republika Srpska where he met with President Radovan Karadzic. Dr. Andolina proposed to treat patients in need of bone marrow transplants in Bosnia. President Karadzic agreed. Soon, he was personally driving trucks and caravans full of medicines into Pale and through the territory of Republika Srpska as well. On the way back, he was taking children to Italy in order to provide them with medical care. This project lasted for approximately six years. During that time, he met with President Karadzic about four to seven times. During such meetings, President Karadzic expressed many times his concern about doing as much as possible to limit the damages of the civilian population resulting from the conflict. He was particularly concerned about the suffering of children of all ethnicities. President Karadzic agreed to facilitate Dr. Andolina's work by allowing him to freely assist children of Bosnian Muslim ethnicity and to transport them across the territory of the Republika Srpska. On May the 5th, 1994, Dr. Karadzic provided him with a letter expressing his support of Dr. Andolina's activities and requested that the authorities extend him all the necessary help in transporting the children of all ethnicities across the territory of Republika Srpska. During 1994, Dr. Andolina was asked by the BH 5th Corps to help children in municipality of Bihac. To reach Bihac, he had to pass through Serbian territories. Dr. Andolina asked permission from Dr. Karadzic, and Dr. Karadzic gave him such authorisation and asked General Tolimir to assist his convoy in order to ensure protection. As a result of Dr. Karadzic's efforts, the lives of several children were saved. And that is a short summary, and I don't have -- at that moment I don't have any question to Dr. Andolina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctor, as you have noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, Ms. Vega Iodice. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Andolina. Yesterday, we met, and I'd like to thank you for that. In paragraphs 5 -- in paragraph 5 of your statement, you -- you stated that you met Mr. Karadzic about four to seven times, and yesterday you told me that these meetings were very brief, were about -- they lasted for about 10 minutes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: As long as I can remember things of 20 years ago, I confirm.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement you also described in paragraph 6 and 7 how Mr. Karadzic facilitated your work in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that without Karadzic's approval, you would have not been able to go through the territory of Republika Srpska with your trucks?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Sure. It would be impossible and very dangerous.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regards to your experience in Bihac, you were asked to bring humanitarian aid because the population in Bihac was starving; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes. That was the request of some members. I don't know which corps, of the Peti Korpus, the 5th Corps of the Bihac army.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And apart from the letter you attached to your statement, the Bosnian Serbs also gave you a medal for your work; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember exactly, but late in the 1990s I -- a sad success. I brought a sick Croatian girl through Srpska, east to west, until Banja Luka. Soon after the Storm operation where most of the refugees were -- were running to east, sometimes burning churches. So they were terrified and upset. So it would be dangerous to bring a Croatian girl through that convoys and so on. And so the Serbian authorities allowed me to keep the girl that reached Belgrade probably by plane, kept the girl in a hospital almost secretly, and then we passed through the territory of Srpska until Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Therein after few minutes she died in the arms of the mother, as requested.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Sorry. And for this reason, I don't remember it was Dr. Karadzic himself or other one gave me a medal since I improved the humanitarian image of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And exactly like you told me yesterday, the Bosnian Serbs used you as a sort of -- for -- for propaganda purposes; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether we could say it's propaganda. Anyway, I -- I helped them to give to the world the best image of -- of themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also met General Tolimir and General Mladic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Yes. General Tolimir was --

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: That -- that's all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Okay. Enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: I'll follow up with more questions. And during these meetings, you never represented the Italian government or any Italian institution; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Not in the 1990s, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And yesterday you also told me about the meeting you had with General Mladic. You met Mladic to facilitate the release of two French pilots who had been taken prisoner; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Another point, difficult to say. So I met Mladic for my safety. In that period I was afraid that he was a little upset since I gave some information about the two French prisoners. So I went to him, so greeted, shaking hands, drinking with him, and assuring him that I was a friend. So mainly for my safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: And I would like to call up 65 ter 24605.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: This is -- this is the official note written by Ljubisa Beara, who was the chief of security of the VRS Main Staff, about the meeting you had on 17th of September, 1995, where you discussed the French pilots and other issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: And if you could go -- we could go to page 2 in the English, and the bottom of page 1 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: On point 3, we can see that you discussed with Ljubisa Beara the issue of the French pilots taken prisoners. You can see that Beara recorded: "Ivic and Andolina have had an idea related to the downed French pilots for whom we agreed that we do not know where they are. When the time comes that we no longer need these pilots and we decide to free them, if we have them, and if they are alive, we shall transfer them to Andolina ..." And as you confirmed --

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: I have no glasses, but as long as I can read, I don't remember completely such document. I never saw it. "An idea related to" --

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: This is a contemporaneous recorded --

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: I don't remember that Ilija Ivic was involved in the freeing -- freeing the pilots. No, I didn't know that they thought about giving to me the French pilots.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: But this is what you proposed them. This was --

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: -- your proposal to them?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page of this document in B --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are hearing French translation. Why don't you show the doctor the first part of this official note again, the first passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: This is, as you can see here, this is an official note that was written by -- by the chief of security of the VRS Main Staff after you met with him. This is a recording that he made of the meeting that he had, as you can see on the first line, with him together with priest Ilija Ivic. And you can see that the official note says: "The priest Ilija Ivic and professor Dr. Marino Andolina, an RS, and Italian citizen, who was awarded the Nemanjic order for his services in the struggle of the Serb people, came to the security administration on 17th of September of this year." Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: No. I remember the medal, yes. Probably the name of the medal I -- I don't know whether it is this medal, but the medal was for the Croatian girl. After really --

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: And if we can look at point -- if you could look at point 1 now, you can see that during this meeting your first proposal to Ljubisa Beara was to work together with him to discover Muslim extremists in Italy, and with that information you would then go to the Italian parliament and bring it down, make it fall?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Oh, yes. This I remember, but later, I think, some member of security forces, probably as acknowledge -- since I cured his son, gave me -- oh, great. Thank you. I guess that about terrorists, as long as I remember, the chief of the security forces of police in Banja Luka or near Banja Luka after -- after a visit of his son gave me as agreement a list of Muslim terrorists or so-called alleged terrorists --

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: -- and then I brought it to the Italian security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And then the last part in the English, beginning of page 2. You could -- you can see that what you told Beara at the time was that you would bring this information to the Italian parliament and say, "You want to bomb the Serbs because the Serbs are terrorists, but the real terrorists are the Muslims."

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: You recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: No, I don't remember these words, of course. I didn't mean that anybody was a terrorist. So I brought a list of Arabs that -- fundamentalist Arabs that were living in Bosnia, nothing else. Names and addresses. I tried to give to the Italian SISMI, but probably was rejected since considered not relevant. And now I am afraid that I brought to the Italian security forces the list of the camps where the -- the Islamic were training the KLA fighters. So for this reason I interfered with Italian politics in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for record, transcript page 10, line 7, bring this information to the Italian parliament and say, and the following should be in inverted commas. So "you" being the Italian authorities. Do you confirm, Ms. Iodice? That's your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It should be: "... bring this information to the Italian parliament, and say," and then it would be inverted commas. That was the quotation from the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You're not tendering this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry, I forgot. I'm tendering this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6148, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two questions, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Andolina, do you remember whether this conversation was recorded?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking about the dangers of travelling through Republika Srpska, are you able to tell us how close to the lines of confrontation did you travel?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: Oh, metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you cross to the Muslim or the Croat side from Republika Srpska? So across the lines.

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: The time when I tried to enter into Bihac, I passed through Croatia to Republika Srpska Krajina and then stopped at Petrovo Selo check-point controlled by the Polish, I guess. Then I stopped since I realised that they are going to kidnap me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Sarajevo? Did you go to the Muslim part of Sarajevo, for example, from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MARINO ANDOLINA
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. IODICE
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I'm not sure whether that was discussed in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. You can move on to another topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no other topics. I just wanted to establish what were the dangers involved, and we established that sometimes he travelled just metres away from the confrontation lines. Thank you, Dr. Andolina, not just for your testimony but for all the things that you did for all the three ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then unless my colleagues have questions for you, Dr. Andolina, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have further witnesses than the next one, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll bring in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the witness take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Jovanovic. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, before you commence your evidence, I must draw your attention to a certain Rule of the -- certain Rule of the procedure and evidence that we have here at the Tribunal, that is, Rule 90(E). Under this Rule, you may object to answering any question from Mr. Karadzic, the Prosecution, or even from the Judges if you believe that your answer might incriminate you in a criminal offence. In this context, "incriminate" means saying something that might amount to an admission of guilt for a criminal offence, or saying something that might provide evidence that you might have committed a criminal offence. However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you and as a consequence you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question, but in that situation, the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony compelled under such circumstances would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence save and except the offence of giving false testimony. Do you understand what I have just told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. Please proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give a statement to my Defence team? By the way, I should ask you and remind myself to speak slowly and make a pause between question and answer. So did you give a statement to my Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up in e-court 1D7237.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see it now before you, Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you read and signed it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the last page, please, so that Mr. Jovanovic can identify his signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After reading it, do you think it reflects accurately everything you've said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to put to you the same questions as you were asked by members of my Defence team, would your answers be essentially the same?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: To the questions asked, the answers would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, may I tender this package to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We're --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Under seal, interpreter's correction. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't believe it was meant under seal. Anyway, we would just like to tender the statement and six associated exhibits. None of them are on the 65 ter list, so we would ask permission to add them because they were provided by the witness after we had filed our exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say six?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you go through one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The first one would be 1D13002, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are not tendering the four items that were objected to by the Prosecution through e-mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're not tendering any of the videos because we're going to lead some of them live, but we understand it's -- yes, we're not tendering the videos as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So could you go through the -- just give us the numbers that you are tendering.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. So I've given you 1D --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Right. The next one we're tendering is 1D13003. And 1D13004, and 1D51000, 1D51001, and 1D51002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about 1D51003? That's also a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct. That's a video-clip, so any of the videos that we will use we will lead live.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just comment? I neither said "MFI" nor "under seal." I'm tendering this package under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Mr. Karadzic did say "under seal."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lines 6 and 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I myself often say that what I didn't mean to say. Any objection, Mr. File, as to these Rule 92 ter statement and the associated exhibits, six of them, that were tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just one brief observation, Your Honour, which is that I noticed recently that 1D13004 is almost a duplicate of D1656, which was admitted into evidence in the Trial Chamber's decision of 4 November 2011. I don't know how the Trial Chamber wishes to deal with that, but I just thought I would note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So if the parties could check there are any other parts that were not included in one -- Exhibit D1656, then those parts should be added to the previous exhibit, i.e., D1656. Otherwise, they will have -- we'll admit the Rule 92 ter statement as well as the remaining five associated exhibits. Shall we give the numbers in lump sum.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The statement will be Exhibit D3007, and the five exhibits will be Exhibits D3008 through to D30012 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Robinson, as to the video-clip that Mr. Karadzic is planning to lead live, the Chamber had the opportunity to take a look at those four items that were objected to by the Prosecution, and the Chamber agrees that it's not relevant in that they provide more information than necessary on crimes not in the indictment. So I'm not sure that we need those items. However, the Chamber is happy to see the video-clip with the number 1D51003. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, should we say something about this? I would like to ask Mr. Robinson to present the view of the Defence concerning these video-clips and their relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I received Mr. Robinson's e-mail as to the relevance as well. My point is that the witness's statement can be understood without these clips and that -- in short, it's unnecessary to receive this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, are you speaking in terms of as an associated exhibit since it's unnecessary as an associated exhibit, or is there any problem with playing it, leading it live and having the witness comment on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I hear from Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- it's our contention that there does not appear to be a claim that -- that these videos are linked in the causality according to the argument that was made in the e-mail by Mr. Robinson. I leave it in the Trial Chamber's hands, though, as to whether Your Honours wish to view the clips in court or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's only marginally relevant, but in any case, in the circumstances, the Chamber will allow the accused to lead live as to those clips. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I shall now read the summary of Mr. Zoran Jovanovic's statement in English. [In English] Zoran Jovanovic was chief of the communications centre in Vlasenica Brigade. Also, he was manager of "Vlasenicke Novosti" magazine. The ethnic structure in Vlasenica where he lived was about 50/50 Serbs and Muslims. The SDS and the SDA were the strongest parties after the elections, followed by Alliance of Reform Forces of Yugoslavia for BH and the SDP. Power was therefore shared between these four parties. Disagreements soon began and these grew with time. The founding of national parties aggravated inter-ethnic relations as they disparaged the other parties, Muslims in particular wanted a sovereign, independent and indivisible unitary BH. Many Serbs were told to go to Serbia as BH was not their country. In 1991, when the war in Croatia broke out and the Muslims supported the Croats in their effort to secede from Yugoslavia, Zoran Jovanovic knew that if they were to succeed, the Muslims in BH would do the same and war would be inevitable. Muslims sent men to Croatia to attend police and military courses. The Muslims did not acknowledge the JNA as the only armed force in Yugoslavia, and the Muslim youth were not sent to the JNA to complete their compulsory service and military training. When a unit of the JNA was mobilised, SDA leaders urged the Muslim members of -- to leave the JNA. The Serbs recognised that war could be prevented if they remained united and told the Muslims this. However, the majority of the Muslim soldiers left the JNA, and it became clear to Zoran Jovanovic that Muslims were preparing for war. At the same time, it was confirmed that the Patriotic League had been established in Vlasenica. Serbs were very worried about the situation in Vlasenica as Muslims were arming themselves and forming military formations. Prominent SDA leaders were procuring arms for Muslims. Information was discovered by the army that demonstrated that Muslims had begun preparing for war much earlier than originally thought. They were made -- they had made plans to destroy buildings and kill or favourably exchange Serbian people. In response to the -- in response, the Serbs then tried to protect themselves by procuring arms. In April 1992, Serbian Territorial Defence from surrounding villages entered Vlasenica and took control of the town. No one was killed in this operation and the Muslims were called upon to hand over their weapons. About 900 weapons were handed in, and in the end of June, up to 2.000 weapons had been surrendered. Negotiations were held with paramilitary formations and a unit of the JNA. However, the situation became more difficult due to debate regarding the division of territory. Muslims and Serbs were moving from one part of the municipality to another depending on the majority ethnic community. In May 1992, Muslims killed eight Serb civilians, two of whom were women. The civilians were on their way to work with the -- when they were killed. Further, Serbs were ambushed during the course of their work. This caused panic and many people, Muslims and Serbs, fled Vlasenica. The municipal authorities attempted to resolve the issue of housing that had been created through the large movement of people around the municipality. Abandoned houses were sealed off and used as accommodation for Serb refugees, but this led to some Serbians feeling embittered. Muslims then attacked neighbouring villages, torching houses and other buildings, taking Serb prisoners, killing many Serbian inhabitants, including elderly people, and plundering property. This happened on a number of occasions to some villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Robinson excused himself. Mr. Karadzic, the fact that I allowed you to lead live the five video-clips does not necessarily mean that the Chamber agrees with its relevance. But because the Chamber didn't have the opportunity to view the video itself, we'll reserve the assessment after seeing the video whether it is relevant and, as such, whether they should be admit the later on. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness be shown 1D51003.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you prepare to explain to us what this footage is and from what time it is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: We can't hear the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] During riots in Vrsinje on the occasion of the Muslim rally in Vlasenica. There are 260 young men in Vrsinje who are ready for liberation of our region. We are all members of the SDA party. We shall fight for independence."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber what this letter U represents that we saw in the last sequence.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This entire footage was made towards the end of August 1991 in a very remote village in upper Vrsinje in the Vlasenica region. This footage proves that at that time when although the war was raging in Croatia and Slovenia, I couldn't even dream there would be a war in Bosnia, but this shows that the Muslims had begun to prepare for the war much earlier than it began, and they are displaying the sign under which they would fight for the liberation they mention in the video. Liberation from whom? From what? Anyway, all this shows that they were preparing for war, to free those territories for their own free Bosnia -- independent Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it would all end in bloodshed, in a bloody settlement of accounts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But what does the letter U mean?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The letter U is a symbol for Ustashas, fascists hordes from the Second World War who perpetrated atrocious crimes in the whole region of Birac and the entire Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise -- you say in paragraph 16 that you recognised some people.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them personally, but I identified them when I got this video-clip with the help of their neighbours who knew them. A friend, Dragan Lukovic, helped me, who is a neighbour of this village Gornje Vrsinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 30, you talk about the attack on Rogosija and then Nedjeljista village that was burnt down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D13005.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you explain to us this video. We have the transcript of the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Prodanovic, we shall ask him to tell us what happened in this village. "My neighbours, Becirevic Hasan, burned down my house. I got out of my house and fled, and through the schoolyard I called for my son Ilija and Nenad Pantic. I called, 'Where are you children? Our houses are burning.' "Behind us is the former primary school in Nedjeljista. You built this together. Muslim and Serb children went to this school. And how are you living this now? "How? There were 70 pupils here, 70 of theirs and only 4 of ours from three villages. Why should I continue to live here if I'm afraid every night somebody will come in and slit my throat."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters have no transcript for this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, tell us who made this video.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The reporter is myself, and the cameraman is Milan, not even trained because we had just got that camera a few days before. It was one of our first videos that we placed in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this, from your knowledge, a solitary incident or was it part of a plan? Did you have any information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Several days before, on the 25th of June, the Serb village of Rogosija was burned down. It had 10 to 12 houses. All of them were burnt down. Even the cemetery was desecrated. And this village is next door to Nedjeljista. And a few days later in June, Nedjeljista itself was attacked. However, in Rogosija and Nedjeljista there were no casualties because people had managed to flee, but all the houses were looted, everything taken from them, and the houses were burnt down in Rogosija. And most of Serb houses in Nedjeljista were burnt down, because Nedjeljista was a mixed village. There were quite a few Muslims very close by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll deal with the video-clips one by one. We'll admit 1D51003. Shall we give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D3013, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I'd like to hear from the parties as to the relevance of the video-clip we just saw, 1D13005. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, may I put a question to the witness? May I put a question to the witness why I showed this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did this reflect on the atmosphere in Vlasenica of both ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the Vlasenica area, in late April, May, June, the situation was such that tensions were increasing all the time. In other words, the overall situation and the relations and life in the Vlasenica area were chaotic. Refugees were arriving from Olovo, Kladanj, Gorazde, especially many of them came in early June from Gorazde when a number of Gorazde people were hurt in an ambush from Rogatica and 30 of them were killed in the ambush. Vlasenica, if I may say, was occupied by refugees, if I may put it that way. In my house, which is 93 square metres, for two or three nights, 30 people were sleeping there in the house. 30 people slept in my house who were refugees from Rogatica. The overall situation and all the relations in Rogatica could be described as chaotic. Of course, this chaotic situation also resulted in - how can I say? - the rage and anger and revolt among a certain number of people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document, which is 1D13003, that relates to Nedjeljista and where it is stated all the things that need to be burned and destroyed and the population killed. Does that refer to the same Nedjeljista that we saw, and was something to that effect done?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: After the torching of Nedjeljista on the 26th, one day afterwards the Serbian forces carried out a counter-attack and drove the attackers away, and in that military action by the Serbian Territorial Defence, a bag was found, an officer's bag belonging to Aljukic Besir [phoen], a lieutenant of the former JNA, a reserve lieutenant, who was in the Territorial Defence with me, because I was also a reserve officer. We knew each other very well. And his notebook was found in that bag, and there was a list in that notebook of his, which I showed to you, where you could see and it was written much before the action that they were preparing what to destroy, who to execute, who to exchange and all of this, and I mentioned all of this in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, this footage from Nedjeljista is accompanying the exhibit 1D13003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All that you are tendering with respect to that video is the clip we saw, the conversation between alleged Prodanovic and Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was looking at that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this footage longer than what we showed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it is a little bit longer, but Ljubo Prodanovic, who died in 1995, he didn't live long, and he left his wife and children behind. I don't know if she's still alive today. To tell the truth, I know his sons who are working in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just a couple of brief points. I think the overarching points that we should remember are, first of all, the Trial Chamber has in the past distinguished between evidence that was presented in significant detail on issues that were considered to be tu quoque and has excluded those, and I think that this falls within that category. I also think that the contention here does not appear to be that the diffusion of the videos themselves led to either increasing tensions or to, as Mr. Robinson said in his e-mail, the killings at Susica, which was -- was the primary issue related in -- to it in argument there. And as a third point I would add that what the witness has just said actually tends to undercut the admissibility of these videos, because he's discussing tensions arising from an influx of refugees, an ambush, and other elements that are not related to the subject matter of the video. I don't think the video aids the Trial Chamber in any meaningful way, and for all of those reasons, I think it should be excluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While the witness's evidence could be understood without this video-clip, I think it lies on the borderline, and since it's a third-party statement which has been confirmed by the witness, on that basis we have a basis to admit it in this case. We'll give the number of it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3014, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, this was in June. In paragraph 31 you talk about an attack on Kljestani and the killing of four elderly people. And this influx of refugees, the killings in the around the area of Vlasenica, how did that reflect upon the authorities in Vlasenica and their ability to deal with this rage that you mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was very difficult. I think that the authorities were almost powerless to deal with the rage of some people who had been expelled from other areas, especially when these killings occurred in the Serbian villages around Vlasenica. Then the rage grew among the villagers of those villages whose inhabitants predominantly lived in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show the witness 1D4144, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're looking at this footage, could you please explain what we're looking at and when and where this was made.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This was made in the Serbian village of Kljestani when four elderly people were killed, two men and two women. They were all older than 60. Of course, they were civilians who were not able to defend themselves. Of course, they were taped here when they were already brought into the house and when the preparations for the funeral already began. And now we're looking at their relatives and neighbours and other people reacting to this killing. The same thing happened on the 15th of August, 1992. On the same day there is another video recording. Fourteen people were killed in the village of Gornji Sadici. We're going to probably see that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at that second part on the same day. That would be 1D41143.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We stop here. I'm struggling to understand the relevance of this clip as such. Why do we need to admit it, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to defer to Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, the Prosecution deserves this, because they asserted that my speech at the funeral in late September was inflammatory and that it led to the commission of crimes. What I'm trying to show here is the position of the authorities, that they have a hand in the crimes, and that other than my speech could anything else have been the cause of the rage among those who perpetrated these crimes. This is something that the Prosecution asked for. Before Rogosija, before the funeral we can see there were two villages where crimes occurred, and from June to late September there were a number of villages that were the victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber finds this clip irrelevant and unnecessary. We'll not admit this. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I show the following, and then I have two more to show to the witness. We can show them and then you decide however you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the transcript of this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, there's no point if we do not hear any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a transcript. There is a transcribed translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we stop here? Did you distribute it to the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the transcript accompanies this exhibit. I thought the participants opened it themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Interpreters are not able to open in their booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Jovanovic, where were these Muslim forces based that made incursions into your villages? Where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: These were mostly neighbours. Most of them were stationed in their villages. For example, close to Gornji Sadici there was the village of Korkutovici. It's still there today. And Cerska was close by, also where there were strong military formations of the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it's important to note, as far as this footage is concerned, that I personally submitted criminal charges some seven or eight years ago against the perpetrators of this massacre and the killing of these civilians to the prosecutor's office of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but they still have not processed the criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the perpetrators are known?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I discovered some of them in my own journalist investigative work. I did have the opportunity to get some information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we are waiting, can we look at 1D5104 while we're waiting to give the interpreters the transcripts. The transcripts are -- are in e-court. I didn't know that the interpreters could not open that. We can play it without sound, and we can ask the witness to explain to us what this footage is and the parties do have the transcript in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Shall we take a break now so that you can provide the interpreters with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. File, how long do you expect your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: 45 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour then. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask this video, 1D4143, to be played again with the transcripts that have now been provided.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] This is the charred corpse of Milivoje Misic. When they caught this Gojko Vukovic, they yelled, 'Hurrah, forward, here is a white-bearded Chetnik. Fuck his Chetnik mother,' you know. We came here and saw ashes and fire. And then we came to extract the corpses. Here we found two corpses. Over there we found a woman whose genitals had been mutilated. She is Peja Misic, the wife of Nedjo Misic. "Zoran Jovanovic: How many people have they killed and massacred? "Around 10 people, I think that 10 people have been buried. With this and Gornji Sadici, 11 houses have been burned, and in the neighbouring village, Jaskovic, five houses have been burned down with no remains. "Zoran Jovanovic: The Muslims did all this? "All of it is done by Muslims, all neighbours, who were on good terms with us prior to this freedom. "Zoran Jovanovic: Samirka Savic. "Samirka Savic: We came here when they started shouting, 'Hurray, fire from the right. Fuck their Chetnik mother.' They started, all with one voice, with the help of shootings from all of the directions. We ran steeply, we left. I didn't cross the creek. The houses were in flames. "Zoran Jovanovic: Jovanka Misic, who was raped, you have to look there at the leg which has been mutilated with a knife. Stabbed in the forehead. Just look how her forehead is. It is a great horror. Next to her is Peja Misic. Look how she was slaughtered. Her throat was slit. They abused her horribly. She was raped in great pain. You see how she is. Look at how she was mutilated. You have to look at it here, people. Pure terror and disgrace."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who made this video?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: My cameraman, and I was with him. On the 16th of August we filmed it, the day after this massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 32, you talk about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I said we'll deal with the video one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, this chain of events of attacks on villages how -- what impact did it have on the situation in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: There was an impact on the population and the people who either hailed or lived in Gornji Nedzarici, and as well as a number of them who had been living in Vlasenica for a while. It had a very negative impact on their sentiment and their overall conduct. With certain individuals, such changes could not even have been controlled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just reiterate my prior objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that we don't need the video in the evidence. What -- what is said in the transcript has been -- in the video has been reflected. We'll not admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. As the last clip, I would like to show the following:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 32, you that say that on the 24th of September, two days prior to the attack on Rogosija, the village of Podravanje had been attacked; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Podravanje is close to the Boksit mine. They had their headquarters in Vlasenica. The attack was carried out on Podravanje as well as the mine itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D51004.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We are merely reading out the transcript as provided by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Doctor: Well, you see, probably in different ways. We have this one here that has been killed by some explosive that had blown up. This one here, both of his legs have been blown off, probably also his head and arm. This one has been run over by a tank or something else. You can see that the chest is crushed, the head shattered. It has almost made flat bread out of his head and body. This one here above, you see both of his legs have been blown off and probably burned along the way. We have this one here behind the door. It is a totally charred corpse, but I have a feeling it had previously contacted some explosives which blew off the arms and limbs, both legs and arms, and that it was later set on fire and completely charred."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you able to form an opinion as to what was the point or need to attack the villages?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Vlasenica municipality, the way I saw it, there was this wish to destroy anything that was Serbian in the environment -- environs of Vlasenica so that Vlasenica town could be completely encircled by Muslim forces. The case of Podravanje where the Boksit mine was attacked, on that occasion the premises of the mine were looted and destroyed. All of the property was taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 26th, it was Rogosija's turn. The funeral was on the 29th of September in Vlasenica. Did you attend the funeral?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement you say that you do not recall my speech. Did anyone tell you that my speech was inflammatory or aggressive? Did people take note of it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have your speech among my documents, and as of late, when I discovered I was to appear as a witness, I looked at it again, and I basically know it by heart. I even have the footage here in case the speech is still not present here. I have the integral version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I seem to have mixed it up. The witness doesn't seem to recall it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I mixed it up. Another witness said that he couldn't recall it. Who recorded the speech?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did partially, and the other part was taken by my cameraman. He wasn't very experienced at the time, so the camera -- the camera moves a lot. In any case, you can be heard as well as those who were in charge of mourning and Velibor Ostojic's address is also on the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was your impression of the speech, Mr. Jovanovic? My speech.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Back then, since I recall it well, my impression was the same as it is now. You were trying to ease the tension to -- to soothe the feelings of the people gathered there and the relatives of those killed. When I heard, for example, that you were charged with causing certain events who took place later on in that -- in those difficult circumstances, I was shaken up as well, because many of my friends and their sons were killed. But if I ever have a comment on that part of the charges, I still see it as a kind of soothing, as a balm which you tried to apply to their wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were people in general familiar with the chain of attacks and crimes? Did people comment on it and how?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, it was well known --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is starting to become leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Excellency. I have no further questions, and I seek to tender the two clips. I'm sorry, you refused to admit the first one. I tender this latest one, the 24th of September, which is five days before my speech.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the same reason, the Chamber will not admit 1D51004. I have to reiterate again that, Mr. Karadzic, it's up to you how to use your Defence time, but I stress that it is not a proper way of court time use to waste time to show the irrelevant exhibit that is not to be admitted. I would like you to consult with Mr. Robinson in the future.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, if we knew what was made part of the indictment and what was left out, the process would have been far shorter. But if we have in the closing arguments by the Prosecution say that my speech was inflammatory and that it brought about certain crimes, then I have to assess all of the evidence accumulatively and put it before you as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is not debating with you, but the Chamber reiterated again that in such a case, even in such a case, you wouldn't need this video. Mr. Jovanovic, as you have noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in most part in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you will be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Jason File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, I noticed that in your witness statement you omitted to mention --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: -- the positions that you held in the VRS during the conflict from 1992 to 1995. It's true that you were a reserve captain in the Drina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And when the Drina Corps Commander Zivanovic set up the Drina Corps press centre on the 19th of November, 1992, he appointed you as one of the first members of the centre; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the head of the information service in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: General Zivanovic also appointed you to the position of war correspondent in the Drina Corps department for moral, religious, and legal affairs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter number -- one moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. He didn't appoint me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be allowed to finish his answer rather than being confronted with a document as if he hadn't said something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was at the head of the information service of the Drina Corps. Its basic task was to inform the public of the events in the Drina Corps, be it in terms of war operations or during periods of lull and in civilian life.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just going to refresh your recollection by looking at a document, which is 65 ter number 24637. Now, we don't have a translation in English, unfortunately, but can you just read starting from the number 1, where it has your name.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Zoran Jovanovic, father's name Tomislav, reserve infantry captain, personal military speciality 31102, register number JTZ, 1951." Which should be the year. "Appointed as a war correspondent in the department for morale, religious and legal affairs, military speciality 31001, captain first class - major."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It will have to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was my point. You didn't ask a question about this. Yes, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am unaware of this document. It is possible that this is how it was drafted as I can see it here. I was acting head of the information service, which means that I wasn't appointed to that position since I was a reserve officer. I was not in that position permanently since I was not an officer. It is possible that this document was drafted as if I were a war correspondent. Indeed, I acted as one because I co-operated with a number of different publications.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So you did perform the duties that are described here as a war correspondent.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: A war reporter would be a better explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6149, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jovanovic, one of the functions of the Drina Corps press centre was to ensure the effective use of propaganda. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And do you recall sending out invitations for seminars in the area of operations of the Drina Corps that were directed at people in charge of so-called information and propaganda?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to the destruction of the Hajrija mosque in Vlasenica which you witnessed because you filmed it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, the Hajrija mosque was destroyed by VRS engineering forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whose forces they were. Most of the people involved are no longer alive. I really don't know whose men they were. It was on the 19th. I remember the date, the 19th of August, 1992. The Drina Corps had still not been established and there were different paramilitary formations milling about. I really don't dare assert that they were the forces of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to read to you the open-session testimony of Witness ST-179 from the Stanisic and Zupljanin case here at the ICTY. It was at transcript 7523 to 7524, on the 11th of March, 2010. There was the question: "Were you aware of the destruction of any mosques in Vlasenica in the summer of 1992?" The answer was: "I knew that this would happen some two or three hours earlier since it was done by the engineering forces of the army. We were given advance notice of some two to three hours in order to make sure that the population living in the surrounding area was evacuated. As soon as we received notice of it, I instructed the policemen to go and inform the population in the surrounding area to leave the general area since we didn't know when the explosion would ensue." "Q. And do you remember, was this the VRS army of engineers or was this the JNA at this stage? "A. The Army of Republika Srpska. And the JNA was no longer there officially by August." Does that refresh your recollection as to the identity of the individuals who were charged with destroying the mosque?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have told you what the situation was like in Vlasenica. When I learned that the Hajrija mosque would be destroyed, I inquired, since I wanted to know why, who, and how, and how much explosives would be used. When they told me the amount, I told them, "That's impossible, people. You're going to level half of the town." They told me to mind my own business. And as a reserve officer, I was in a situation to ignite a hundred grams of TNT, but the amount they wanted to use would raze half of the town. I am still of the opinion that whoever ordered it to be carried out that way wanted to have half of the town destroyed. My camera was on a tripod, and because of the blast it was knocked over.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, you had -- you had obtained film of two Muslims standing in front of the mosque the day before it was destroyed saying that it had not been desecrated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it had not been.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, you went on Republika Srpska television in the middle of September, and you showed a clip of two Muslims standing in front of the mosque the day before it was destroyed, and you said that: "This was the best proof that claims of all those who wanted to characterize Serbs as barbarians and destroyers of sacred sites were false." That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about it. Do you have that footage?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like you to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are relying on something I don't know about. You say that I talked to some people and that I showed it. Perhaps there were conversations like that, but I don't think I ever had it broadcast under such circumstances, especially not after the mosque had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like to refer to 65 ter number 24633. Now, what you'll see from this is that this is an excerpt from an anthology of papers from a conference on the 1991 to 1999 wars in Yugoslavia, which was held in Belgrade on the 7th to the 9th of November, 2001. And if we could go to English page 2, B/C/S page 5.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we be told who set it up, who set up that panel discussion?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm proceeding through the document now with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I think the question was related to the provenance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: This document is a -- is an anthology of papers. It was -- it was originally admitted as a Defence exhibit, DH1600, in the Hadzihasanovic case. I should say this is -- what we're showing is an excerpt from that. The total ERN range that was admitted into evidence in the Hadzihasanovic case was Y005-2655 to 2707.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was the conference about?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It was on -- the title of the conference, Your Honour, is "1991 - 1999 Wars in Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask what the basis is for this question to be raised in cross-examination, because this mosque in particular does not form part of my indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's related to the credibility of this witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So you'll see that the chapter we're talking about here is called "The Destruction and Devastation of Islamic Community Buildings in the Aggression Against BH 1991 - 1995." And I'd like to direct the Court's attention to English page 4, B/C/S page 6. In the B/C/S we're actually going to look at the left-hand side at the bottom, the penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, this paragraph says: "Those who planned the destruction of the more prominent mosques, prior to doing so, they would bring, under threat, selected Bosniaks to testify in front of the said mosque that it was not desecrated and they would video-tape this testimony for a story about that site. Such recorded material was then kept and broadcast at the right moment. That was the case with the Hajrija, a stunning mosque in Vlasenica. Mid-September 1992, a story about this mosque was broadcast on Bosnian Serb TV in which two Bosniaks were standing in front of this mosque and testified that it had not been desecrated. On that occasion, journalist Zoran Jovanovic said that this was the best proof that claims of all of those who wanted to characterize the Serbs as barbarians and the destroyers of sacred sites were false. Of course, the truth was totally different; namely, the recording was done one day before that mosque was destroyed, and it was broadcast about 20 days after it had been destroyed." Now, Mr. Jovanovic, isn't that an example of precisely the type of propaganda you were trying to teach other so-called journalists to use in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, no --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we all deserve to know who said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, this is absolutely untrue, the stuff written in the book. It is absolutely untrue. Absolutely. Give me proof. Show me footage. We'll find it. Does it exist? I know everything I recorded in the four years, and I still have it. It is absolutely untrue. Absolutely. It couldn't even take place. I'll use an example of propaganda, because I saw some newly created journalists who for different reasons came to the information services in the Drina Corps. On one occasion I told them the following: In order for you to understand what propaganda is in war, what it means to inform at a time of war, I will quote Churchill, and I paraphrase: The truth in times of war is so precious that it has to be accompanied by a bodyguard of -- by bodyguards representing lies. As journalists, you seem to be writing reports as if everything were a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, I think we're straying away from the subject of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. Let's collapse the B/C/S and let's see the first page of English. Yes. This says an anthology of papers, discussion from the round table. Next page, second page. It says page 369, 370. And then page -- next page, page 3. And it continues, 371, 372. And page -- next page. And the font has been changed, and it's in a different format, and I can't follow what it is about, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm happy to explain, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: The existing translation that we had for this document did not include these final three paragraphs on page 370, and so we requested those paragraphs to be translated, and I provided the existing translation for context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you may answer the question from the accused. Is it a paper or is this an excerpt of somebody's speech at the conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We believe this is a paper that was presented at this conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who said, or who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: The author's name is on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Show us the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: B/C/S page -- page 5. Muharem Omerdic. It's on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's page 369, and the author's name was not translated in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I don't think there's any B/C/S text around the author's name that could be translated. It's just the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So author's name was omitted in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I believe that's correct. I also believe that that translation starts further down the page on page 369.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It started from the highlighted part.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think I have to say too much, Mr. President, but apart from the issues of reliability, this is a third-party statement in 2001 that the witness has not confirmed in any way. So under your practice, it wouldn't be admissible even if it was even a somewhat less unreliable document than it appears to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: May I be heard, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would it not be related to the credibility issue, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's a relevant document, there's no doubt about it. But it's a statement of a third party just like those that you have excluded in the past. So it's been put to the witness. He made a statement about it, and he hasn't confirmed anything about it, and it shouldn't be admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. This is a very technical issue on the part of lawyers. Just a second. Yes, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I don't believe it's a statement. It's a paper from a conference, and I also would rely on Rule 94 for a document that has been admitted into evidence in a previous trial. I think that satisfies at least the issue of authenticity, and I think that this -- because it is directly on point to the witness's testimony and his function in this trial, I would contend this should go to weight as opposed to admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think for judicial notice of authenticity we need some other requirements, but I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Following the practice of the Chamber, we'll not admit this at this stage, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'd like to look at paragraph 4 of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say something, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're actually -- we're going to move on to another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Jovanovic. We did not admit this, and if necessary, Mr. Karadzic will take up the issue later on. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like to turn --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: -- your attention to paragraph 4 of your statement, where you say: "The ethnic structure in Vlasenica before the war was about 50/50, Serbs and Muslims, with a few Yugoslavs, Roma, Croats, and other ethnic minorities. According to the 1991 census, Vlasenica municipality had about 33.000 inhabitants." You still stand by that statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to the last Muslims, there were -- there was a smaller majority of Muslims, but nobody was over 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can we look at 65 ter 242L, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You'll see that this is a copy of the 1991 census that you cited in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If we could go to e-court page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask about this document? We are again using exclusively a Croat document speaking to warring parties. This is a Croatian document. Bosnia has its own documents on census. Croatia was one of the warring parties in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I -- I find this intervention inappropriate, Mr. Karadzic. I think you can take up that issue in your submission later on, or you can come back with Bosnian statistics if necessary. Let's continue, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, on this page you can see the entry for Vlasenica. In the first column, you have the total 1991 population listed as 33.942.
