So your statement appears to be close to that exact number. Then further columns have the population divided into Croats, Muslims, Serbs, Yugoslavs, and others, and you have some percentages. Now, looking at the Muslim and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let's collapse the English. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Looking at the Muslim and Serb categories, you see Muslims were 55 per cent of the population and Serbs were 42 per cent of the total population. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So you would acknowledge that what you said in your statement and again here today, that the population was 50/50 Serbs and Muslims is an exaggeration. It was Muslims held an absolute majority with 55 per cent and Serbs representing 42 per cent.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I as a journalist always used the relevant data. The census of 1991 you are showing me, I heard this data. I didn't know you were going to ask me this. I could have brought this myself. Never once was it adopted by any competent organ of Bosnia. The 1991 census was done very randomly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Pardon me for interrupting, but you cited the 1991 census in your own statement as support for the number of inhabitants; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Maybe I did invoke it, and I did say it was the 1991 census, but I never recognised it and I never used it in my work as a journalist. I relied on the previous 1981 census and the earlier ones from 1971 and 1961. It would be very interesting to analyse all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So just to clarify, when you said in your statement that the ethnic structure in Vlasenica before the war was about 50/50 Serbs and Muslims, what we were supposed to understand from that was that you meant the ethnic structure in Vlasenica before the war, i.e., in 1971, was about 50/50 Serbs and Muslims. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. In my mind it's always been 50/50, except before the Second World War, before the killings in the Second World War when there was a Serb majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about paragraphs 23 and 24 of your statement where you talk about a debate that was raging in the Vlasenica Assembly on the division of territory into Milici municipality, Serbian Vlasenica, and Muslim Vlasenica. You go on to say that Muslims and Serbs were moving from one part of the municipality to the other depending on where their ethnic community was the majority. You said the Muslims were in the northern part towards Cerska, while the Serbs were in the south. Now, in 1991, the Muslims were also the majority in Vlasenica town and many villages surrounding that. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: In Vlasenica itself, yes. There were more Muslims. I don't know exactly, but that is also in the statistics from 1991. Except I'm not quite sure it was exactly true because of that campaign that was led in 1991, but the surrounding villages around Vlasenica are majority Serb, around the town. I can enumerate these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about towns like Drum and Zaklopaca. Those were predominantly Muslim towns.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Zaklopaca itself, the centre of Zaklopaca, is Muslim. Around Zaklopaca are Serb villages. The same goes for Drum.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. So I'd like to ask you about paragraph 29 of your statement where you say: "The municipal authorities formed a holding centre for Muslims in facilities belonging to the TO in the Susica suburb to protect them from attacks by Serbs who had been expelled and who came from various areas. I once went to the facility to take cigarettes and other supplies to some of my friends. I asked what it was like for them there, and they replied that it was not that bad because no one was disturbing them." So first of all, you personally went to the Susica camp; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Only that once, to bring cigarettes and some food.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And while you were there, you met Dragan Nikolic who was running the camp; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. I did not meet with Dragan Nikolic that time. I met with Veljko Basic, an old retired policeman, and I asked him to let me take what I had brought to those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You're aware of who Dragan Nikolic is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that Dragan Nikolic, but I didn't see him that time, the only time I visited. Later on I had no more time. I had other work. I was on other assignments. I didn't see him that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, you're aware that Nikolic pled guilty before this Tribunal for crimes committed at Susica; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And do you know that the judgement in that case that was rendered on 18 December 2003, found that the hangar where the detainees were housed was severely overcrowded and the living conditions were deplorable. Whole families were kept there, including women, the elderly and children as young as eight. Many of the detained women were subjected to sexual assaults including rape, and that Nikolic admitted his personal involvement in the killing of nine people, torture, and facilitating the sexual assault and rape of women by allowing guards, soldiers, and other males to have access to these women on a repeated basis and encouraging sexually abusive conduct. So my question to you is: When you talked to these friends that you describe and you say that they told you it was not that bad because no one was disturbing them, who exactly are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: One used to be the owner of the dry cleaners in Vlasenica. I'll try to remember his name. He confirmed what I quoted earlier. I'm trying to remember his name. I didn't expect this question. Very soon after that, he was transferred to Batkovic in a larger group. What you've just told me I never heard on that occasion or later from relevant witnesses. Even that Dragan Nikolic whom I saw a few times later never spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let's be more specific. During your time at Susica, did you ever stand by and watch a woman get raped?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Never. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we have - and this is not to be broadcast - 65 ter number 24643, please. We're not broadcasting because of the identity of a rape victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: This is a doctor's referral of a patient to a specialist, dated 17 September 1993. I'm just going to read to you the relevant parts of this. "In the middle of April 1992, my daughter was staying with my father near Susica camp. I was at home. Six Chetniks came. They were armed. They ordered me to run to the camp. It was my neighbour Radenko Krstic who gave me the order. They brought me to the camp. They sent me to the guard's house where they were recording personal data and taking belongings. Dragan Nikolic and Zoran Jovanovic were present there. They ordered Pero Djuric from the Elastik to search me. They put me in the hall. I was forced to sit on concrete. In the evening, Dragan Nikolic came and pointed an automatic rifle at me and ordered me to stand up. He led me to the camp yard and demanded that I tell him where my brother was. I told Pero Djuric to kill me. They beat me, mistreated me and told me that they had killed me husband. They beat me terribly. Using a knife they carved some letters on my body. "The second evening, Pero Djuric and Dragan Nikolic led me outside again and took me to the guard's house. There was a bed and a chair there. They interrogated me once more. Then Dragan Nikolic went outside and Pero Nikolic told me, 'You are in my hands now, bitch.' He raped me there in front of Zoran Jovanovic. The others sat around watching what he was doing and laughing." I'll stop there.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Question --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Do you recall that episode --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is incredible how flagrant this lie is, with this Dragan Nikolic and Pero Nikolic, people I generally know. I never spent five minutes together during the war anywhere, let alone in Susica. This is unbelievable. I read on Muslim web sites all sorts of blatant untruths targeting me, but I'm honestly shocked that anybody could have written this. This has absolutely nothing to do with the truth. That I watched this scene described here, it's incredible, especially because I did not spend five of minutes together during the war with Dragan Nikolic and all the other people named here. Perhaps I spent 2 minutes together with Dragan Nikolic in some war zone somewhere. This is incredible, Mr. Prosecutor. Especially since I don't know this woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But I don't have any clue that Zoran Jovanovic referred to in this document is the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, the witness has at least confirmed that he was present in the -- in the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Again this is the statement of a third person. You see the date of September 17th, 1993, on the second line below the name and so it's not a contemporaneous statement. So under your practice it -- and it's certainly not been confirmed by the witness. Under your practice it wouldn't be admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything, Mr. File?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, in fact, I'll just move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I just have a few questions about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much longer would you need? I think your time is almost up.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I only have about four or five more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, after 1995, when you were the manager of Radio Vlasenica after the conflict, did you ever announce on a broadcast that General Ratko Mladic was a great man whose role in Bosnia's war was to keep Islam from spreading across Europe?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I still think that today, if that's what you're asking. Now, whether I said it, whether there was a radio show discussing that, whether journalists made a report or a programme where that was mentioned, I don't remember, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: These fine. You co-authored a book in 2010, with a second edition in 2012, called "Srebrenica, What Really Happened." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Srebrenica, How it Really Happened." That's the title of the book, not "what really happened" but "how it really happened."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And do you stand by everything in that book?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, and will make more books. I'm a fighter for the truth. We want the truth. I don't want to cover up any Serb crime, but I don't want crimes against Serbs covered up. I'm sorry that your Office of the Prosecutor took over all of that material but never proceeded with any investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Do you stand by the statement in the foreword to the book by Peter Priskil, and I'm quoting now: "Srebrenica in its official version is a propaganda lie that will not become the truth however loudly and frequently it is repeated." And it goes on to say: "The propaganda Srebrenica is NATO's Auschwitz fake." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was written by Peter Priskil, a German from Freiburg, based on the facts that he was able to obtain. I, as an individual, am trying to prove that the shameless lie called Srebrenica -- and I'm not saying that there were no crimes by Serbs, but they were not the way they are portrayed, and you will soon have opportunity to find out the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that wasn't my question. My question was: Do you stand by that statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That it's a shameless lie, yes, but the comment is his vision which is close to my heart, but I couldn't call it the absolute truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Would you call the propaganda Srebrenica is NATO's Auschwitz fake?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's his definition. At the end, when all this is over, we'll see what it really is. This is Priskil's statement. What things really are we will find out after all the inquiries that are yet to be completed, but we will never give up on finding out the truth as long as we are alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. File. Do you have any re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions. I'll conclude soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovanovic, you were asked about propaganda or information work. I want to ask you, did you establish as a journalist that along with the armed conflict there was also a propaganda war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. We Serbs lost the media war. Why? Because our people who were supposed to think about that were unwilling to pay for the truth. We all thought the truth would prevail, and we still think that today. But for the truth to prevail, a lot, a lot of money is needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When there was discussion about the destruction of the mosque, in your view was this mosque destroyed professionally and with minimal purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Totally unprofessionally as far as I'm concerned. And concerning that conference and what was said there, I never wrote a single line in any publication, not a single letter. Why? Because it was done so badly that half of my hometown was destroyed, and I was appalled by all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the authorities or the involvement of the authorities in Vlasenica in this event?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I was there on the spot. Nobody from the authorities was anywhere in the vicinity, nor did I see any evidence later that anyone from the local authorities of Vlasenica had been involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not said that the witness said: Nor did I hear later about any of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that case will probably feature in one of my books that I've been writing over the past few years, and the footage that survived will find itself in some documentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic [sic], is it correct what you said that you did not hear then nor later than any of the authorities were involved in this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the fact that this destruction occurred on the 19th of August, what about that event? How does that stand in relation to the other events, what happened on the 15th of August, what happened on the 16th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just before you answer the question. Yes, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: First of all, it's a leading question, but more importantly, it's straying away from the credibility issue that was explored on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I think that the credibility of this witness has not been disturbed. I'm just asking what were the motives for the destruction of the mosque. This was suggest -- it was suggested that this was done by the professional service of the engineering corps of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last sentence by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the destruction of the mosque itself is not relevant as far as it relates to the cross-examination. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will leave that topic then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, you were not on the SDS list. You were on the list of a reform --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Alliance of the Reform Forces of Yugoslavia for Bosnia and Herzegovina whose president at the time was Ante, Ante. He recently died. I forgot his name for the moment. And the person --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is beyond the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- representing Bosnia-Herzegovina was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, no. I need to be allowed to complete -- the questions are 50/50. I mean, it's a question of the number of the population of the citizens since there are doubts cast as to the census here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just don't see how his political party membership is relevant to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So what did you say? Who was the head at the level of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was Nenad Kecmanovic for Bosnia and at the level of Yugoslavia it was Ante Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And there were -- were there other Serbs in that party of yours and in other parties that were not the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were, in the Reform Forces and the SDP. This was the former League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who won the elections in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: The SDS had 27 deputies, the SDA had 26, the Alliance of Reform Forces 4, and the SDP 3. That was the number per party. There were a total of 60 deputies in the Municipal Assembly. Among the four representing the Reform Forces, I was among them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the last two questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript should say "SDA 26." Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you and Serbs in other ethnic groups were voted for mostly by their relatives, how do you explain the victory of the SDA if the census is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: This is a leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The SDS, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, and you are asking me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: SDS, not the SDA. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: These are -- this is a line of leading questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, it's not important to me. I will leave that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Are you going to reformulate it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I can rephrase it. The Serbian electorate was divided among a number of parties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you view the SDS victory in relation to the census data?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I tried to comment on that a little bit already. I know that that census from 1991 was never officially adopted by B and H organs or the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica because that was how the process of adopting the census results went. There was also a fierce campaign regarding the census, who would be the signatories in which villages. And I would say that there were also some machinations regarding that census. It is a fact that the SDS won in the Vlasenica municipality where according to the votes by -- along ethnic lines, voting for the SDA or the SDS, the distribution should have been different, regardless of these parties that were leaning toward the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And my last question to you, Mr. Jovanovic, is this, although the document was not admitted but it was probably admitted somewhere else. It says in the document that in mid-April 1992, her daughter was captured and so on and so forth. In mid-April, did you have the opportunity to see that there was Susica for Muslims, and did you go to Susica in mid-April?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: I forgot to say that. It didn't exist in mid-April. The only visit that I made to Susica was in early June, the 3rd or 4th of June. I was there one single time, and I even think that I have it written down somewhere when this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in mid-April, was Susica set up to receive Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellencies. I have no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. You could have been in the SDS. It's a pity you weren't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to thank the Trial Chamber if there are no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Until when did you remain in the Drina Corps, Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was demobilised on the 27th of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Jovanovic. On behalf the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish you all the best. Thank you, Mr. President. The best of luck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are there any matters to be raised? I take it there's no witnesses for the remainder of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. There's nothing to raise on our part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There are then two matters I'd like to raise at this time. First, on the 15th of February, 2013, the Prosecution raised with the Chamber its concern related to the potential identification of a protected witness by the accused on the 14th of February, 2013. The Chamber has considered this issue as well as the submissions made by the parties on the 15th of February, 2013. Taking into account the situation raised by the Prosecution, the Chamber takes this opportunity to reiterate its position related to the disclosure to the public, including other witnesses, of any confidential witness information. As held in paragraph 34(1) of the "Decision on Protective Measures for Witnesses" dated 30th of October, 2008, the accused is not prevented from disclosing confidential information to a witness as long as the disclosure is directly and specifically necessary for the preparation and presentation of the case. The Chamber reminds the accused that this may only be done for limited purposes and in exceptional circumstances. In relation to the specific instance on the 14th of February, the question posed by the accused did not require the transcript of the protected witness testimony to be read out to the witness on the stand. Further, since this witness on the stand had earlier testified that he did not know about the situation being referred to, there was no need to refer to the protected witness's evidence at all. Furthermore, going into private session was not sufficient to protect the identity of the said witness from the witness on the stand. Therefore, the Chamber reminds the accused to be especially diligent in its efforts to ensure that the accused is complying with the Chamber's orders related to the protective measures assigned to the witness. The next matter is related to the Defence Rule 92 ter notifications. The Chamber has already reiterated its position on the Defence submitting numerous versions of Rule 92 ter notifications and witness statements and the necessity of only submitting a draft version and a revised version of such document in a timely manner. The Chamber is now also concerned with a recent trend which has emerged and which has resulted in a loss of time and resources for the Chamber and all parties to the proceedings. There have been a number of instances recently where on the day of a witness's testimony, the Defence drastically reduces number of associated exhibits sought for admission when this exercise could, and should, have been done when the revised version of Rule 92 ter notification is filed, once Mr. Karadzic or another member of the Defence team have proofed the witness in question. This has happened even when the Prosecution has not objected to the specific associated exhibits. While the Chamber very much appreciates the Defence tendering only those associated exhibits which the Defence deems absolutely necessary, it encourages the Defence to conduct this exercise at the time the revised Rule 92 ter notification is filed so as not to use the Chamber's and Prosecution's time and resources for no good reason. The accused is encouraged to focus and tender only those exhibits which are really of significance to the case against him and to avoid tendering peripheral documents through 92 ter statements which he then ultimately decides not to tender or even use with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I say something about first issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to assure you, Your Excellencies, that it's in my best interest to have an exemplary transparent process and that I will never deliberately violate the confidentiality. This is something that can only happen out a failure to understand the technicalities. As for the second question, probably Mr. Robinson would give you a better reply, but I do know that we are very restrictive and conservative in terms of what the witness knows about a certain document, so that is why we avoid presenting anything that has not been thoroughly checked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just bear in mind what I told you. Unless there's anything further, the hearing is adjourned. We will resume on Tuesday next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of February, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.06 p.m.,
